chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## The Mine-to-Magnet Gap

Rare earth permanent magnets—specifically sintered neodymium-iron-boron—are the silent enabling technology inside F-35 actuators, electric-vehicle traction motors, wind turbine generators, and industrial robots. For the better part of three decades that supply chain has run almost entirely through China, which controls roughly 90 percent of global sintered NdFeB production. USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR), headquartered in Stillwater, Oklahoma, was assembled to close that gap from both ends simultaneously: a domestic magnet factory drawing on a domestic heavy rare earth mine, with no link in the chain touching Chinese territory. As of the frozen snapshot date of May 23, 2026, USAR is the only US-listed pure-play spanning mine, metal, and magnet—a positioning that has attracted a $1.5 billion private investment round, a pending $2.8 billion Brazilian mine acquisition, and a Q1 2026 cash balance of $1.75 billion while the Stillwater plant has just begun shipping its first commercial orders.

## Two Anchor Assets

USAR's platform rests on two geographically separated assets. The first is the **Round Top deposit** in Hudspeth County, far west Texas—leased from Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (TMRC)—which hosts 16 of the 17 rare earth elements, with an unusually heavy skew toward dysprosium and terbium, the high-coercivity dopants that keep NdFeB magnets stable at elevated temperatures. Round Top also carries gallium, beryllium, hafnium, lithium, and uranium, giving it a critical-minerals profile that stretches well beyond magnets. In December 2025, USAR [accelerated its commercialisation timeline by two years](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/10/3203137/0/en/USA-Rare-Earth-Accelerates-Timeline-for-Round-Top-Deposit-Commercial-Production-by-Two-Years.html), targeting first commercial output in late 2028 against a prior 2030 schedule. In January 2026 the company selected Fluor Corporation and WSP Global as EPCM partners to advance a Definitive Feasibility Study, with completion targeted for early 2027. A hydrometallurgical demonstration facility under construction in Colorado is expected to run 2,000–4,000 hours of solvent-extraction circuit testing through 2026, generating the flowsheet data the DFS requires and, USAR argues, saving "tens of millions of dollars" versus conventional piloting.

The second asset is the **Stillwater sintered NdFeB magnet plant**: 310,000 square feet of manufacturing floor on the southern Oklahoma prairie, described by management as the first scaled US-domestic sintered NdFeB facility. On March 26, 2026, USAR [commissioned Phase 1a of its Stillwater production line](https://www.mining.com/usa-rare-earth-commissions-new-magnet-production-line-at-oklahoma-plant/), enabling commercial order fulfilment beginning in the second quarter of 2026. Phase 1a targets an annual run-rate of 600 metric tons by Q4 2026; Phase 1b, expected online in Q1 2027, doubles that to 1,200 metric tons per annum. The long-range nameplate target remains 5,000 tpa, the scale at which USAR's unit economics and government offtake theses become self-sustaining. The Stillwater workforce already exceeds 100 employees; magnet operations are led by Bob Fredette, whom the company describes as one of the leading sintered NdFeB experts in the United States.

## Heritage and the Path to Market

USA Rare Earth was organised privately around 2019, drawing on the exclusive lease rights to Round Top that TMRC had accumulated over the prior decade. Joshua Ballard—appointed CEO in December 2024—steered the company through its NASDAQ debut via a business combination with [Inflection Point Acquisition Corp II](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001787434/000121390025001750/ea0227098-425_inflection2.htm), which closed in March 2025. Ballard departed in October 2025, succeeded by Barbara Humpton, the former chief executive of Siemens USA and board member of the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, whose appointment signalled a shift from founder-operator mode to industrial scaling. CFO William Robert Steele Jr. joined in June 2025. Also in November 2025, USAR [closed the acquisition of Less Common Metals Ltd.](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/18/3189795/0/en/USA-Rare-Earth-Closes-Acquisition-of-Less-Common-Metals.html) (LCM), a Cheshire, UK-based producer of rare earth metals and strip-cast alloy that is the leading ex-China supplier in its category, inserting a metal-making link between Round Top oxide and the Stillwater magnet line. LCM also carries established relationships with European and allied-nation defence primes.

## Financials: First Revenue, Heavy Burns

FY2025 marked the transition from zero-revenue development to nominal commercial operations. Product revenue of [$1.643 million appeared in Q4 2025](https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:8c9c73e460b1b:0-usa-rare-earth-reports-fy2025-results-1-64m-revenue-in-q4-359-9m-cash-year-end/) — the first in company history — against a full-year GAAP net loss of $297.6 million and an operating loss of $59.5 million. Year-end cash was $359.9 million. A going-concern note accompanied the December 2025 disclosures, but was effectively extinguished in January 2026 when USAR [closed a $1.5 billion PIPE](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/USAR/usa-rare-earth-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-g9fu5eye8xfs.html), vaulting the balance sheet to $1.75 billion in cash by March 31, 2026. Q1 2026 revenue rose to $5.7 million on gross profit of $0.1 million (gross margin 1.9%), with a net loss of $67.0 million and capex of $38.6 million as Stillwater commissioning spending peaked.

CEO Humpton framed the quarter in terms that signalled industrial ambition over near-term profitability:

> "The first quarter of 2026 was a period of fundamental transformation for USA Rare Earth, defined by the successful execution of our $1.5 billion PIPE financing and the announcement of an agreement for the 100% economic consolidation of our Round Top project."

On April 20, 2026, USAR announced a definitive agreement to [acquire Serra Verde Group for approximately $2.8 billion](https://investors.usare.com/news-releases/news-release-details/usa-rare-earth-announces-definitive-agreement-acquire-serra) ($300 million cash plus 126.85 million shares), adding the Pela Ema mine in Goiás, Brazil — described as the only producer outside Asia capable of supplying all four magnetic heavy rare earths at commercial scale — and a 15-year US Government-backed offtake agreement. The deal, expected to close in Q3 2026, is outside the frozen window but casts a long shadow over the dossier's open questions.

## The Strategic Context

Underpinning each of USAR's capital raises is Beijing's willingness to weaponise the rare earth supply chain. China imposed intermittent dysprosium and terbium export controls through 2024–2025, spiking spot prices and jolting Western defence procurement officers. The US Congress legislated a January 1, 2027 deadline banning Chinese-origin NdFeB magnets from defence systems. That deadline sits approximately seven months from the Stillwater Phase 1a commissioning date — a tight window that amplifies USAR's first-mover value for defence customers but compresses the timeline for quality qualification and ramp. MP Materials (NYSE: MP), the other major US rare earth company, is scaling a competing magnet plant in Fort Worth, Texas, backed by a $400 million DoD equity investment and price-floor purchase commitments; it represents the principal domestic benchmark against which USAR's Stillwater economics, customer conversion, and Round Top feasibility progress will be measured.

The dossier that follows interrogates each link in the chain: how Stillwater scales from 600 to 1,200 and ultimately 5,000 metric tons; how customer letters of intent convert to binding offtake before the 2027 defence deadline; how Fluor and WSP's DFS shapes Round Top's capital requirements and permitting timeline; how a $1.75 billion treasury translates against the multi-hundred-million-dollar capex road ahead; and whether USAR's competitive positioning relative to MP Materials and a rapidly internationalising peer set — now including Serra Verde — supports the mine-to-magnet thesis at the valuation implied by its post-PIPE capital structure.

chapters.title: From 2019 private founding through Inflection Point business combination to mine-to-magnet US supply chain
chapters.body:
## A Texas Mountain and a Missing Supply Chain

The founding thesis of USA Rare Earth was less a mining story than a manufacturing one. When Pini Althaus, the company's founding chief executive, assembled the vehicle that would eventually reach NASDAQ, the strategic problem he was trying to solve was not the scarcity of rare earth deposits in the United States — geologists had catalogued dozens — but the absence of any scaled domestic capacity to convert those ores into the sintered neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnets that sit at the heart of electric-vehicle traction motors, wind-turbine generators, and the propulsion systems of the F-35 and the Virginia-class submarine. China controlled roughly ninety percent of global sintered NdFeB production. The gap between the raw material in the ground and the finished magnet on the shelf had never been bridged in the United States at commercial scale. USA Rare Earth was built to bridge it.

The corporate lineage traces to November 20, 2018, when an Australian shell vehicle called Morzev Pty Ltd. signed an option agreement with Texas Mineral Resources Corp., a small public company that held two nineteen-year mining leases from the Texas General Land Office covering approximately 950 acres on and around Round Top Mountain in Hudspeth County, far West Texas. Within months, Morzev nominated USA Rare Earth, LLC as the operating optionee, and the private predecessor entity was formally constituted in 2019 with Althaus at the helm. The structure of that founding agreement set the financial architecture for everything that followed.

## The Round Top Lease: Texas State Land and the TMRC Joint Venture

Round Top Mountain rises 380 metres from the Chihuahuan Desert floor roughly eight miles northeast of Sierra Blanca, a rhyolite dome that geologists would come to regard as one of the most mineralogically complex rare-earth-bearing deposits in North America. Its host rock carries sixteen of the seventeen rare earth elements, with an unusually favourable weighting toward the heavy rare earths — dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium — that command premium prices and are subject to the most acute supply-chain anxiety in Western capitals. The deposit also contains economically significant concentrations of lithium, gallium, beryllium, hafnium, and uranium, providing a critical-minerals co-product thesis that would later become central to the company's permitting and funding arguments.

The mineral rights underlying Round Top sit on land owned by the State of Texas and administered by the General Land Office on behalf of the Texas Permanent School Fund. TMRC held its surface and mineral access through the GLO under two nineteen-year leases, and the state extracted a 6.25 percent net smelter royalty on all minerals produced — a first-priority claim that USA Rare Earth would carry on its balance sheet as a permanent cost of production. TMRC's own commercial interest was structured as a retained equity stake: under the 2018 option agreement, USA Rare Earth could earn a seventy-percent interest in the project by spending $10 million in two tranches — $2.5 million on rare-earth separation and purification optimization, then up to $7.5 million on a bankable feasibility study — with an option to acquire an additional ten percent for a $3 million cash payment. By May 2021, when TMRC and USA Rare Earth formally contributed their respective assets into Round Top Mountain Development, LLC, that exercise had been completed and the joint venture stood at eighty percent USA Rare Earth to twenty percent TMRC.

The same month, USA Rare Earth closed a $50 million Series C financing advised by Goldman Sachs and BMO — the capital that would fund the early permitting work, geotechnical studies, and, more critically, the decision to plant a magnet factory in the American heartland before the mine had produced a single tonne of ore. A 2019 preliminary economic assessment had estimated the project's net present value at approximately $1.56 billion, and a resource estimate of 364,000 tonnes measured and indicated plus 735,000 tonnes inferred gave the company the geological confidence to begin committing capital to downstream manufacturing.

## The Stillwater Decision: Manufacturing First

In June 2022, USA Rare Earth announced an investment of more than $100 million in a sintered NdFeB magnet manufacturing facility at Stillwater, Oklahoma. The choice of Stillwater — a mid-sized university town roughly sixty miles west of Tulsa — reflected both a favourable labour market and the kind of state and municipal support that had proved elusive elsewhere: the Oklahoma Department of Commerce committed $1.2 million, and the City of Stillwater structured a tax-increment-financing arrangement worth up to $7 million, repayable from the project's future property-tax increment. The company took 310,000 square feet at 100 West Airport Road and began installing the powder-formation, jet-milling, wet-pressing, machining, coating, and magnetisation equipment that sintered NdFeB production requires.

The rationale for sequencing manufacturing ahead of mining was deliberate and commercially pragmatic. Magnet customers — defence primes, EV traction-motor Tier 1 suppliers, wind-turbine OEMs — had spent the better part of a decade articulating demand for a non-Chinese supply of sintered NdFeB. What they could not source was a qualified domestic supplier with certified production and a traceable, audited supply chain. USA Rare Earth calculated that establishing the Stillwater plant, qualifying its magnets with defence and commercial customers, and building the revenue base from processed ore purchased on the open market would de-risk the path to project finance for Round Top far more than any purely mine-focused development strategy. The mine would come; the magnet factory would come first.

The original 2023 production target slipped, and the build-out extended across 2023 and 2024 under chief executive Tom Schneberger, who had succeeded Althaus as the company transitioned from exploration-stage to construction-stage operations. On December 17, 2024 — with the SPAC combination three months from closing — the board installed Joshua Ballard as chief executive. Ballard brought no mining background: his curriculum vitae ran from the University of Iowa, where he had studied Russian, through the Thunderbird School of Global Business, to a decade at private equity firms investing in Eastern Europe, then to six years as chief financial officer of Energy Recovery Inc., a NASDAQ-listed industrial manufacturer. His appointment signalled that the company considered itself, at that moment, a manufacturing and capital-markets problem rather than a geological one.

## The Inflection Point Business Combination

The vehicle chosen to take USA Rare Earth public was Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. II, a blank-cheque company that had raised $250 million in gross proceeds from its May 2023 IPO, placing 22 million Class A ordinary shares at $10 apiece into a trust that stood at $251.25 million. The merger agreement between IPXX and USA Rare Earth was signed in August 2024, ascribing an $800 million pre-money equity value to the private predecessor — an $870 million pro forma enterprise value for the combined entity.

What followed illustrated, with unusual clarity, the structural fragility of the post-2022 SPAC market. At an extraordinary general meeting on November 18, 2024, called to extend the combination deadline, IPXX shareholders holding 22,794,651 Class A shares elected to redeem at approximately $10.83 per share — surrendering roughly $247 million and leaving barely $23.9 million in the trust. The company responded by aggressively building its concurrent private investment in public equity. The PIPE that had been struck at signing for approximately $25 million was upsized to $40.75 million on February 4, 2025, and expanded by a further $8 million at the moment of closing, assembling what the company described as nearly $50 million in committed private capital.

Stockholders approved the combination on March 10, 2025. The transaction closed three days later, on March 13. On March 14, USA Rare Earth began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker **USAR**, with its public warrants — exercisable at $11.50 per share — listed separately as **USARW**. Total gross proceeds from the trust and PIPE at closing reached approximately $65 million; cash on the balance sheet as of March 31, 2025 stood at approximately $23.4 million, reflecting the rapid deployment of PIPE proceeds into Stillwater commissioning.

## First Magnets and the Road to Mine-to-Magnet

By January 2025, as the SPAC paperwork was advancing toward its final vote, the Stillwater facility had produced its first prototype sintered NdFeB magnets — still at laboratory scale, but sufficient to begin the qualification process with industrial customers. Phase 1a of the plant formally commissioned in March 2026, enabling commercial-grade production with a nameplate capacity of approximately 600 metric tonnes per annum by the fourth quarter of 2026, with the Phase 1b build-out targeting 1,200 tonnes annually by early 2027. The ultimate design envelope of 5,000 tonnes per annum remained the benchmark against which management calibrated the thesis: at that scale, Stillwater would represent a meaningful fraction of projected US defence and commercial NdFeB demand.

Round Top's definitive feasibility study was assigned in January 2026 to Fluor Corporation and WSP Global as engineering, procurement, and construction management partners, with commercial mining production targeted for 2028. The same month, the US Commerce and Energy departments extended a non-binding letter of intent for $277 million in direct CHIPS Act support plus a proposed $1.3 billion senior secured loan — a federal endorsement of the mine-to-magnet thesis that Joshua Ballard described as validation of "years of capital and operational commitment to delivering a supply chain that the United States has never had."

On March 5, 2026, the company announced that it would acquire TMRC's remaining approximately 18.6 percent interest in Round Top Mountain Development LLC, exchanging 3,823,328 shares of USAR common stock — valued at approximately $73 million at the prevailing price — for full ownership of the deposit. The transaction, subject to TMRC shareholder approval, was pending at the frozen snapshot date. If it closes, it will complete the consolidation of the asset that Pini Althaus optioned from a Texas state-land-office lease in 2018 into a single, fully integrated corporate structure — the mine, the magnet factory, and the listed vehicle holding them, all under one roof.

## The Rhyolite and the Sintering Line

Round Top Mountain rises from the Chihuahuan Desert of Hudspeth County, West Texas, roughly eighty miles east of El Paso, a surface-exposed rhyolite laccolith whose unweathered flanks stretch more than a mile in base diameter. The geology is unusual: late-stage fluorine vapors percolated through the intrusion after emplacement, substituting rare earth elements into the calcium lattice of fluorite minerals — principally yttrofluorite and yttrocerite — rather than concentrating them in the carbonatite or phosphate matrices typical of light-rare-earth deposits. The substitution mechanism strongly favours the heavy end of the lanthanide series. The result is a deposit that carries approximately seventy percent of its total rare earth oxide content as heavy rare earths and yttrium, a distribution almost without parallel in the Western Hemisphere.

A 2019 Preliminary Economic Assessment prepared by Gustavson Associates under Canada's NI 43-101 standard classified a resource of 1.034 billion tonnes at 639 parts per million total rare earth oxide — 359 million tonnes in the Measured and Indicated categories and 675 million tonnes Inferred. At a proposed mining rate of 20,000 tonnes per day, an open-pit operation would touch only 14 to 18 percent of the resource over a 20-year economic plan, implying a potential mine life extending beyond a century. Because the deposit outcrops at surface, the strip ratio is effectively zero.

The 2019 PEA modelled annual production that translates the HREE enrichment into economic terms: 1,642 tonnes of yttrium oxide equivalent, 197 tonnes of dysprosium oxide, 22 tonnes of terbium oxide, and meaningful output of the light-magnetic rare earths neodymium (174 t/yr) and praseodymium (65 t/yr). The Gustavson team projected initial capital expenditure of $350.4 million — including a 25 percent contingency — and derived a pre-tax net present value at a 10 percent discount rate of $1.564 billion, an internal rate of return of 70 percent, and a 1.4-year payback period. As the late TMRC chief executive Dan Gorski remarked in 2019, "for less than the cost of a single Navy F-35C fighter jet, the Round Top mine could be brought into production."

### A Multi-Commodity Ore Body

What distinguishes Round Top from a narrowly defined rare-earth project is the portfolio of co-products embedded in the same ore. The 2019 PEA modelled annual production of 8,956 tonnes of lithium carbonate, 109 tonnes of beryllium hydroxide, 42 tonnes of gallium oxide, 39 tonnes of hafnium oxide, and 75 tonnes of uranium oxide. The deposit has been characterised as the richest known US occurrence of gallium and beryllium, and it hosts eleven of the thirty-five minerals the federal government has designated critical to national security. In the post-2024 geopolitical environment — in which Beijing has periodically restricted dysprosium and terbium export licences and moved to constrain gallium and germanium flows — the co-product breadth of Round Top takes on strategic weight beyond its rare earth grades alone. Texas awarded the project a $14.2 million grant from the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund in May 2026, citing projected job creation of approximately 260 positions in Hudspeth County and more than $1.4 billion in capital investment in West Texas.

### From Ore to Oxide: The Round Top Flowsheet

Unlike the Mountain Pass carbonatite — which requires elaborate cracking chemistry to liberate cerium, lanthanum, and the light rare earths from bastnasite — Round Top's yttrofluorite mineralogy is soluble in dilute sulphuric acid. The extraction flowsheet centres on a heap-leach operation: ore will be crushed to approximately half an inch, stacked on a lined pad, and irrigated with dilute sulphuric acid at a target pH of 1.0 to generate a pregnant leach solution carrying the dissolved rare earth load. Column-leach testing conducted by Resource Development Inc. in 2020 demonstrated a 6.3-fold concentration increase in rare earth elements relative to the feed material after elution over approximately three bed volumes — results that support the capital efficiency of the open-pad architecture relative to pressure-leach or roast-leach alternatives.

Separation from the pregnant leach solution was originally designed around continuous ion exchange and continuous ion chromatography (CIX/CIC), the same class of technology the company operated at its Wheat Ridge, Colorado hydrometallurgical demonstration facility — opened in June 2020 as the first facility in the United States to separate the full rare earth elemental range since the late 1990s. More recent technical communications describe five continuous solvent-extraction circuits targeting a 2,000-to-4,000-hour continuous operating campaign, with focus elements of dysprosium, terbium, hafnium, and zirconium. The hydrometallurgical facility at Wheat Ridge was targeting commissioning by the second quarter of 2026.

In January 2025, USA Rare Earth announced that it had produced dysprosium oxide from Round Top ore at 99.1 percent purity — verified by an ISO 17025-accredited laboratory — the first demonstration of domestic heavy-rare-earth oxide production from the deposit at commercially relevant purity. "We're excited about the progress we've made in bringing this processing capability back home to the United States," said chief executive Joshua Ballard at the time.

The feasibility timeline accelerated materially in December 2025, when management pulled the commercial production target forward by two years to late 2028. A pre-feasibility study is expected in the third quarter of 2026, with a definitive feasibility study to follow by the first quarter of 2027, targeting an eventual 40,000 metric-tonnes-per-day mining rate.

### The Stillwater Plant: Sintered NdFeB at Scale

The second anchor of the mine-to-magnet thesis sits in a 310,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma. The plant was built around equipment acquired from Hitachi's former North Carolina magnet operation — described by management as "the only scalable, sintered neodymium-iron-boron manufacturing system in the Western Hemisphere" at the time of acquisition. The Innovations Lab, the facility's R&D and prototyping wing, was commissioned on 31 March 2025. Phase 1a, the first commercial production line, was commissioned on 26 March 2026.

The sintering process for NdFeB magnets is a sequence of tightly controlled steps, each of which requires oxygen exclusion and precise thermal management. At Stillwater, the upstream alloy-making — strip casting of neodymium-iron-boron master alloy from molten metal and the subsequent hydrogen decrepitation (HD) that fractures the cast flake into coarse powder — is performed by Less Common Metals at its Hooton Park facility in Ellesmere Port, Cheshire, a 67,000-square-foot plant that USA Rare Earth acquired in November 2025 for $100 million cash plus 6.74 million shares. LCM operates two strip casters installed in 2012 and 2013, an HD furnace commissioned in 2020, and six vacuum-induction furnaces for rare earth metal and alloy preparation from oxide feedstock.

The HD powder arrives at Stillwater for jet milling: the coarse flake is further comminuted to individual powder particles of three to five microns in an inert-atmosphere jet mill, producing single-crystal-domain particles whose magnetocrystalline anisotropy is the source of the magnet's coercive force. The fine powder is then wet-pressed in a magnetic alignment field into large green blocks. Those blocks undergo high-temperature sintering — densification under vacuum at temperatures approaching 1,000 to 1,100 degrees Celsius — followed by multi-step annealing cycles that optimise grain-boundary microstructure. The sintered blocks are then precision-machined to customer-specified geometries, coated for corrosion resistance, and magnetised in a pulsed field. The Innovations Lab additionally carries grain-boundary diffusion capability, which allows post-sintering infusion of heavy rare earth elements into the magnet surface to elevate coercivity for high-temperature applications without proportionally increasing bulk Dy or Tb loading.

| Capacity Milestone | Output | Target Date |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1a commissioned | First commercial production | March 2026 |
| Phase 1a + 1b combined | 1,200 metric tonnes per annum | Q1 2027 |
| Full facility (four lines) | 4,800 metric tonnes per annum | Multi-year buildout |

Target applications span the highest-value end of the permanent magnet market: EV traction motor magnets requiring elevated coercivity to survive under-bonnet temperatures; wind turbine direct-drive generators for which the rare-earth-per-megawatt intensity is highest; defence weapons systems including the F-35 and Virginia-class submarine programmes; and the rapidly expanding robotics and physical-AI actuator market.

> "Today's announcement is a major step in delivering on our ambition to build a global champion and the partner of choice in rare earth elements, oxides, metals and magnets," said chief executive Barbara Humpton on the day Phase 1a commissioning was announced.

### Bridging the Gap: The Vertical Integration Timeline

The mine-to-magnet thesis rests on the premise that Round Top REO will one day feed Stillwater magnets. That closed loop remains a medium-term aspiration rather than an operating reality as of the May 2026 snapshot. The near-term feedstock solution runs through three nodes: LCM in Ellesmere Port, which supplies strip-cast NdPr alloy enriched with Dy and Tb sourced from non-Chinese channels; the Australian Strategic Materials tolling framework signed in March 2024; and, most significantly, the Serra Verde rare earth operation in Goiás, Brazil, whose acquisition USA Rare Earth announced in April 2026 for $2.8 billion in cash and stock. Serra Verde's Pela Ema mine is currently the only scaled non-Asian producer of all four magnetic rare earths simultaneously — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium — with current annual output of approximately 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes of total rare earth oxide and a Phase 1 target of 6,400 tonnes per year by end-2027. A US government-backed special-purpose vehicle holds a 15-year offtake agreement for the entirety of Phase 1 magnetic REE production.

The full integration path — Round Top ore through heap leach and solvent extraction to rare earth oxide, oxide reduction to metal at a planned US metals plant, strip casting at LCM or its successor, jet milling and sintering at Stillwater — is projected to converge no earlier than the late 2020s, when Round Top commercial production commences and domestic metal-making capacity has been established on US soil. Until then, Serra Verde and LCM constitute the supply bridge. The strategic logic is that the supply chain segments need not all operate domestically from day one, provided that each link is held outside Chinese jurisdiction and that Round Top ultimately closes the oxide-to-magnet loop with US-mined, US-separated feedstock.

## A Thin Trust and a Market That Had Seen This Before

When the business combination between Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. II and USA Rare Earth LLC closed in March 2025, the newly listed USAR began trading on the Nasdaq with a capital structure that carried the marks of its moment. The SPAC wave of 2020–2021, which had briefly channelled billions of dollars into mining and clean-tech ventures, had by 2025 left investors deeply wary of blank-check vehicles: redemption rates on late-cycle SPACs routinely exceeded 90 percent, and the rare earth sector in particular had accumulated a graveyard of underfunded aspirants. USA Rare Earth entered the public market aware that its trust cash — whatever survived the redemption window — would be insufficient on its own to carry the Stillwater, Oklahoma sintered neodymium-iron-boron plant through commissioning, let alone fund the Round Top, Texas deposit toward bankable feasibility.

The trust structure of Inflection Point II, like most SPACs of its vintage, was designed to hold cash in short-dated Treasuries pending shareholder vote. SPAC shareholders who disagreed with the merger — or simply preferred to take their cash and interest rather than accept the inherent dilution of the combined entity — redeemed their shares at approximately net asset value per share before the close. Industry patterns across critical-minerals SPACs in the 2023–2025 cohort suggested that companies entering such combinations with anything above 20 to 30 percent trust retention were beating the odds. The specific redemption figure for Inflection Point II has not been publicly disclosed in granular form within the proxy documents filed on EDGAR, but the company's subsequent capital-raise activity — including the reliance on PIPE proceeds and follow-on equity discussions — implied that trust cash alone provided a limited runway: likely in the range of tens of millions of dollars rather than the hundreds of millions the company's capex ambitions would ultimately require.

## The PIPE as the Real Opening Balance Sheet

The practical opening balance sheet for USAR was therefore the PIPE — the private investment in public equity commitments that closed concurrently with the business combination. PIPE investors in critical-minerals SPACs through this period were largely a specialised cohort: commodity-focused hedge funds, family offices with direct exposure to defence supply chain themes, and, increasingly, institutional investors tracking the US-domestic reshoring of strategic materials. The PIPE for the Inflection Point II / USA Rare Earth transaction provided committed capital that partially offset redemption outflows, giving the company a working base from which to fund Stillwater plant commissioning and near-term corporate overhead.

The company entered its first full quarter as a public entity carrying the overhead structure of a pre-revenue industrial manufacturer: G&A reflecting newly public-company compliance and investor-relations costs, ongoing R&D related to magnet alloy optimisation and processing, and construction and equipment spend at the Stillwater facility. Operating losses in the early quarters of public life were therefore structural — not a signal of strategic drift, but the expected profile of a company in the capital-deployment phase before magnet revenue begins to compound.

## Capex Anatomy: Stillwater First, Round Top Later

The capital requirements bifurcate cleanly into two tranches with very different timelines. The Stillwater, Oklahoma plant — the first-priority spend — is a sintered NdFeB magnet manufacturing facility targeting an initial nameplate capacity of approximately 1,200 metric tons per annum. At that scale, industry precedent for greenfield sintered magnet capacity in the United States suggests plant-and-equipment cost in the range of $100 million to $200 million for fully built-out initial-phase infrastructure, though the precise figure depends heavily on the extent of in-house alloy production versus toll processing, press and sinter furnace count, and the degree of vertical integration into magnet surface finishing. USA Rare Earth has indicated an expansion path from 1,200 tpa toward 5,000 tpa; that step-change in capacity would require additional capital deployment likely in the $150 million to $300 million range, consistent with the linear cost-per-ton economics observed at comparable facilities.

Round Top represents a longer-dated, far larger capex event. The heavy rare earth deposit in Hudspeth County, West Texas — operated under exclusive lease from Texas Mineral Resources Corp. — contains meaningful concentrations of dysprosium, terbium, yttrium, and a suite of other critical minerals, but advancing from the current resource characterisation and preliminary economic assessments toward a bankable feasibility study, environmental permitting, and mine construction is a multi-year process with capital requirements that could reach several hundred million dollars at full mine-plus-separation plant scale. That spend sits well outside the near-term runway horizon and is contingent on feasibility results, permitting timelines, and the availability of project-level debt financing — most plausibly through the Department of Energy Loan Programs Office — that would not be drawn until construction decisions were made.

## The Federal Funding Stack

The federal funding thesis is central to how management has framed the company's capital path, and it has genuine policy substance behind it. The Department of Defense, operating under the Defence Production Act Title III authority, has directed material grant funding toward domestic magnet manufacturing as part of its rare earth supply chain resilience programme. The most directly comparable precedent is MP Materials' Fort Worth, Texas magnet plant, which received approximately $35 million in DoD DPA Title III support in the initial tranche — federal money that helped de-risk the capital raise for that facility. USA Rare Earth has positioned itself as an eligible recipient of analogous DoD grant funding, given that sintered NdFeB magnets are direct inputs into the F-35 programme, Virginia-class submarine systems, and a range of other weapons platforms whose supply chains the Pentagon has explicitly designated as critical.

The Department of Energy Loan Programs Office pathway is more conditional. The LPO has been active in critical-minerals infrastructure through the IRA era, extending conditional commitments and loan guarantees to battery materials, lithium processing, and rare earth separation projects. For USA Rare Earth, an LPO facility would most naturally apply to Round Top mine and separation plant development rather than to the Stillwater magnet plant — the latter being more analogous to manufacturing than to resource extraction infrastructure. An LPO conditional commitment, if obtained, would not translate to cash immediately but would materially improve the company's ability to raise project-level debt and reduce equity dilution at the mine development stage.

The IRA Section 45X advanced manufacturing production tax credit adds a unit-economics dimension to the picture. Section 45X provides per-unit production tax credits for qualifying advanced manufacturing outputs, and Treasury guidance has addressed coverage for critical minerals and their derivatives. To the extent that sintered NdFeB magnets qualify under the applicable product categories, the credit would accrue on a per-kilogram basis once the Stillwater plant reaches commercial production — functioning as a margin support mechanism rather than upfront capital. The specific credit rate and qualification pathway for fully finished sintered magnets versus magnet precursors remained a subject of active regulatory interpretation through the snapshot window.

## Dilution Mathematics and the Warrant Overhang

The post-SPAC capital structure carries a warrant overhang that any investor modelling USAR's equity value must size carefully. Inflection Point II issued public warrants and private placement warrants as part of its original SPAC structure; those warrants survive the business combination and typically carry exercise prices set at a premium to the SPAC trust NAV — often $11.50 per share in the standard SPAC template. When the common stock trades below the exercise price, the warrants are out of the money and function as latent dilution. When the stock rallies, warrant exercise creates share issuance that caps price appreciation absent simultaneous revenue proof points.

On top of the warrant overhang, the company's pre-revenue capital needs mean that additional equity issuance is a near-certainty across the 2025–2027 period. At-the-market offerings, registered direct placements, and follow-on public offerings are the most likely mechanisms. Each of these raises dilutes existing shareholders, and in the context of a small-cap company with a still-thin float, even modest raise sizes can create meaningful per-share dilution. The discipline with which management sequences its equity raises — prioritising non-dilutive federal grants before returning to the equity window — will be a key determinant of long-term shareholder returns.

## The MP Materials Comparison

| Metric | MP Materials (MP) | USA Rare Earth (USAR) |
|--------|------------------|----------------------|
| Listed | Aug 2020 (SPAC / Fortress Value Acq.) | Mar 2025 (SPAC / Inflection Point Acq. II) |
| Primary asset at listing | Mountain Pass mine (CA) — mining + LREE concentrate | Stillwater OK magnet plant + Round Top TX deposit |
| Magnet plant | Fort Worth, TX (announced 2022, commissioning 2024–25) | Stillwater, OK (commissioning 2024–25) |
| DoD DPA support received | ~$35M initial tranche (Fort Worth) | Targeted; grant applications filed |
| Initial magnet nameplate capacity | ~1,000 tpa (Fort Worth Phase 1) | ~1,200 tpa (Stillwater Phase 1) |
| Capex scope | ~$700M total (Mountain Pass + Fort Worth combined) | Est. $100–300M (Stillwater); multi-hundred-million (Round Top) |
| Revenue at listing | ~$170M (mine concentrate) | Pre-revenue (magnet) |
| IRA 45X eligibility | Pursued (magnet output + alloy) | Pursued (magnet output) |

MP Materials' trajectory offers both encouragement and a cautionary note. Mountain Pass gave MP a cash-generating mine business from which to cross-subsidise Fort Worth's construction — a financial cushion USA Rare Earth does not have in equivalent form, since Round Top's mine revenue lies years away. The Fort Worth magnet plant itself required roughly three years from announcement to initial commercial magnet shipments, a timeline that underscores the engineering complexity of standing up sintered NdFeB capacity at scale. On the positive side, MP demonstrated that DoD willingness to commit grant funding to a domestic magnet manufacturer was real and material, not merely aspirational policy language.

## Cash Runway and the Revenue Conversion Imperative

Management's ability to stretch its opening capital base through the pre-revenue period depends on several simultaneously moving variables: the pace of Stillwater commissioning and first commercial magnet shipments, the conversion of customer letters of intent into binding offtake agreements that support project finance and lender confidence, the timing of any DoD DPA grant disbursement, and the stock price trajectory that determines whether equity raises are dilutive at punishing levels or at levels the company can absorb.

The tightest near-term risk is the gap between current cash — trust residual plus PIPE proceeds, reduced by G&A and construction spend from the March 2025 close onward — and the date at which Stillwater begins generating meaningful magnet revenue. China's intermittent dysprosium and terbium export restrictions through 2024–2025 have raised the strategic premium on non-Chinese sintered NdFeB supply and sharpened customer urgency around signing offtake. That macro tailwind does not guarantee contract conversions on timelines that fit the cash model, but it improves the negotiating leverage significantly.

The company's pre-revenue operating loss cadence — G&A, D&O insurance, stock-based compensation, and R&D — is manageable in absolute dollar terms for a small-cap industrial, likely running at $15 million to $30 million per annum depending on headcount and public-company infrastructure build-out. The more significant cash consumer is Stillwater construction completion and the tooling and materials required to run qualification and sample programmes for defence and EV customers whose procurement processes can stretch twelve to twenty-four months from first sample to commercial purchase order. Every quarter that bridges the gap between current cash and commercial revenue is a quarter that either requires new capital or draws down the buffer that separates a funded development company from a distressed one.

chapters.title: Quarterly cadence through 2025-2026 capital deployment and commissioning
chapters.body:
## The First Days Public: Q2 2025

The business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. II had barely settled when USA Rare Earth disclosed its first earnings report as a NASDAQ-listed company in August 2025. The second quarter ended June 30 with $121.8 million in cash and no significant debt — a position that reflected both the SPAC trust proceeds and the post-closing warrant activity that would define the company's idiosyncratic capital cadence for the next several quarters. Revenue was effectively nil; the company remained squarely in a pre-commercial deployment phase, channelling capital toward steelwork and equipment installation at the Stillwater, Oklahoma sintered NdFeB magnet plant while its commercial team signed non-binding paper at pace.

Joshua Ballard, who had shepherded USA Rare Earth from its 2019 private founding through the March 2025 NASDAQ listing, framed the quarter as a demand-validation exercise rather than a financial one.

> "We are seeing a surge of customer interest as we prepare to begin production at our Stillwater, Oklahoma magnet facility in early 2026."

By 11 August 2025 the company counted twelve memoranda of understanding and joint development agreements representing approximately 300 tons of annual production across aerospace and defence, data centre cooling and industrial motors, and automotive electrification customers. More than seventy active commercial engagements were in flight. Ballard sharpened the message: "we have the potential to sell out our first 1,200-ton production line prior to commissioning its full capacity." The operating loss for the quarter was $8.8 million; a statutory net loss of $142.7 million was dominated by non-cash changes in the fair value of the $169 million warrant liability and $100 million earnout liability that are standard artefacts of post-SPAC balance sheets rather than cash consumption. Cash used in operations was $7.9 million, a number management consistently referenced to characterise real burn. Commissioning at Stillwater was targeted for the [first quarter of 2026](https://investors.usare.com/news-events/news-releases).

## The LCM Turn: Q3 2025

The third quarter, covering July through September 2025, became a pivot both in strategy and in leadership. Cash had climbed to $257.6 million by September 30, partly from a $125 million common-equity PIPE and partly from warrant exercises, and management noted that subsequent to quarter end the balance had crossed $400 million — providing an early signal of the capital-raise cadence to come. The operating loss widened to $15.9 million as headcount and project-development spending accelerated; the GAAP net loss for the nine-month period reached $247.4 million, again heavily distorted by non-cash fair-value movements.

The operational headline was the announcement, alongside Q3 results in early November 2025, of a definitive agreement to acquire Less Common Metals Ltd. (LCM), the Cheshire, UK-based manufacturer of neodymium-praseodymium and samarium-cobalt metals and strip-cast alloys. LCM represented the only proven ex-China producer of both light and heavy rare earth permanent magnet metals and alloys at industrial scale. Deal terms called for $100 million in cash and 6.74 million shares of USAR common stock. For Barbara Humpton, who had replaced Ballard as chief executive on October 1, 2025, the acquisition was the conceptual keystone of the company's integration thesis.

> "With the downstream capabilities of our magnet manufacturing plant in Stillwater well underway, which is now complimented by the metal making and strip casting capabilities of LCM, we are closing the loop within the rare earth magnet supply chain. Our strategy all along has been to take the steps necessary to secure the supply chain with the critical know-how and capabilities from mine all the way through magnet manufacturing."

Humpton arrived from Siemens USA, where she had presided over a business generating more than $20 billion in annual revenue. Board chairman Michael Blitzer described her as "a transformational and visionary leader." Humpton herself put the mission in national security terms: "there is nothing more critical to national and global security than securing a domestic supply chain for rare earth minerals and magnets." Ballard remained with the company in a consulting capacity through October 31, 2025. On the technical side, Q3 also marked the identification of a processing flowsheet for Round Top, validated through bench- and pilot-scale testing, underpinning a targeted pre-feasibility study completion in the second half of 2026.

## Closing the Loop: Q4 2025 and the January PIPE

LCM closed on November 18, 2025. USA Rare Earth finished the calendar year with $359.9 million of cash and $1.643 million in revenue — the first recognised commercial sales, principally derived from LCM's established rare earth metal contracts with European defence and magnet manufacturers. Gross profit was $195 thousand, implying a gross margin of 11.9%; operating expenses for the full year reached $59.7 million and operating cash consumption was $49.0 million.

The fourth quarter was, however, primarily a capital-structure quarter rather than an operational one. On January 29, 2026 — three weeks after Q4 ended — the company closed a $1.5 billion private placement of approximately 69.8 million shares of common stock at $21.50 per share. Inflection Point anchored the offering; Cantor Fitzgerald acted as lead placement agent and Moelis as co-placement agent. The PIPE was linked to a non-binding letter of intent from the U.S. government, and closing the raise satisfied a key milestone under that arrangement. Post-transaction cash stood at roughly $1.75 billion — roughly ten times the prior year-end level.

Humpton framed the full year in retrospective terms at the Q4 release on March 30, 2026:

> "2025 was the year that USA Rare Earth set the foundation to execute our integrated rare earth growth strategy."

She added a forward marker: "With the definitive documentation for our $1.6 billion Department of Commerce funding expected to be completed in April 2026, the Company will be exceptionally well capitalized." Phase 1a at Stillwater was confirmed commissioned in March 2026; the facility was expected to begin fulfilling sintered NdFeB orders in the second quarter of 2026 and ramp toward 600 metric tons per annum (MTPA) by year-end, with Phase 1b targeting 1,200 MTPA in Q1 2027. Fluor Corporation and WSP Global were selected as engineering-procurement-construction-management partners for the broader site. LCM, meanwhile, was on course to expand to 3,000 MTPA of metal and alloy capacity by end of 2026.

| Quarter | Cash (period-end, $M) | Revenue ($M) | Operating Loss ($M) | Net Loss ($M)† | Key Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 2025 | 121.8 | — | 8.8 | 142.7 | 12 MOUs/JDAs; 70+ engagements |
| Q3 2025 | 257.6 | — | 15.9 | 156.7 | LCM deal; CEO transition to Humpton |
| Q4 2025 | 359.9 | 1.6 | 59.5 (FY) | 297.6 (FY) | LCM closed Nov; Phase 1a built out |
| Q1 2026 | 1,750 | 5.7 | 36.7 | 67.0 | $1.5B PIPE closed Jan; Phase 1a commissioned Mar |

*†Net loss figures include large non-cash movements in warrant and earnout fair values.*

## Q1 2026: Commissioning, Serra Verde, and the Capital Stack Assembled

The first quarter of 2026 was the quarter in which pre-commercial status formally ended. Revenue of $5.7 million — largely LCM metal sales — carried a thin gross margin of 1.9%, reflecting start-up overhead at Stillwater and initial LCM integration costs. The operating loss was $36.7 million and the GAAP net loss $67.0 million; capital expenditure was $38.6 million, the heaviest single-quarter construction spend in the company's history as Stillwater's Phase 1a installations reached completion. Cash used in operations was $18.6 million.

The strategic register, however, was dominated by deal announcements rather than line items. In March 2026, the company announced a definitive agreement to acquire Texas Mineral Resources Corp. (TMRC), the lease-holder that had originated the Round Top deposit in Hudspeth County, Texas, and which had held the exclusive lease position that USA Rare Earth had been operating under since the private predecessor era. Absorbing TMRC gave the company 100 per cent economic control of Round Top rather than the lease-and-royalty structure that had prevailed. A preliminary feasibility study was now targeted for Q3 2026, a definitive feasibility study for Q1 2027, and commercial production from the mine for late 2028 — a pull-forward of roughly two years against prior guidance. The State of Texas awarded $14.2 million from its Semiconductor Innovation Fund against a projected $1.4 billion capital investment and approximately 260 jobs at the Round Top complex.

In April 2026, USAR announced a definitive agreement to acquire Brazil's Serra Verde Group for approximately $2.8 billion. Serra Verde operated an ionic clay deposit in Goiás State and held the distinction of being the only scaled producer of all four magnetic rare earth oxides — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — outside Asia. A fifteen-year offtake agreement with price floors was embedded in the transaction structure, providing a supply-assurance floor for the integrated value chain.

Humpton crystallised the first-quarter narrative at the May 13, 2026 results call:

> "The first quarter of 2026 was a period of fundamental transformation for USA Rare Earth, defined by the successful execution of our $1.5 billion PIPE financing and the announcement of an agreement for the 100% economic consolidation of our Round Top project. By securing a definitive agreement to acquire Serra Verde, the only scaled producer of all four magnetic rare earths outside Asia, we are closing the loop on our integrated global value chain."

The proposed $1.6 billion Department of Commerce collaboration — structured as milestone-based capital reimbursement — remained in final documentation as of the May 2026 reporting date, with completion now targeted for that month. Between the PIPE proceeds, the anticipated government facility, the Texas grant, and the LCM revenues, USA Rare Earth had in the span of four quarters after its NASDAQ listing assembled a capital stack that dwarfed the modest SPAC trust it had closed with in March 2025. The task the company now faced was converting that stack into tonnes of sintered magnet delivered against the MOUs and JDAs that had accumulated in its commercial pipeline since the first days public.

---
